sentences.text:
Applicant :- Nitin Gautam
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Ashwini Kumar Tripathi,Sr. Advocate,Yashaswin Venugopal Bajpai Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ajay Kumar Pandey,Jay Prakash Yadav Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Manish Tiwary, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sei Ashim Luthra, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Satish Trivedi, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Ajay Kumar Pandey,
learned counsel for the informant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 99 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 302 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sector-24 Noida, District Gautam Budh Nagar during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased on 14.05.2019 and at the time of marriage huge dowry was demanded by the applicant and thereafter his marriage was performed with the deceased but applicant and his parents were not satisfied with the dowry given by the informant i.e. father of the deceased and they always harassed her for additional demand of dowry and on 17.04.2022 applicant informed the informant that his daughter i.e. deceased has committed suicide by hanging herself.

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation of demand of dowry and torture made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and only being husband of the deceased, applicant has been made accused in the present matter along with his parents.
5. He further submits that actually wife of the applicant i.e. deceased was having a very erratic behavior and on the date of incident some dispute arose between husband and wife with regard to cooking food and subsequently she committed suicide.

He further submits that immediately after the incident applicant rushed her to the hospital but doctor declared her dead and the fact that applicant has taken the deceased to the hospital is even evident from the inquest report, which has been annexed along with instant bail application.
6. He further submits that even after the incident applicant informed the informant and this fact is admitted by the informant in the FIR and these facts shows the bonafide of the applicant.

7. He further submits that although in the FIR and in the first statement of the informant recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. no specific allegation of demand of dowry was made but when his second statement was recorded by the Investigating Officer then he stated that applicant and his family members demanded Scorpio car and this fact further suggests that subsequently informant developed a new story with regard to demand of dowry and initially on the basis of vague demand of dowry FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his parents.

8. He further submits that from the perusal of the account statement of the deceased i.e. wife of the applicant, which has been annexed along with supplementary affidavit dated 17.07.2023 filed by the applicant, it appears that number of times applicant transferred the amount in the account of his wife and there was absolutely no occasion for him to make demand of Scorpio car.
He further submits that there is no evidence on record till date which can show that soon before her death deceased was ever tortured by the applicant due to demand of dowry.

He next submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 17.04.2022 i.e. for more than a year.
9.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submits that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within three years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and applicant failed to explain the death of his wife.

10. Learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the informant further pointed out that as deceased had already died, therefore, only to show his bonafide applicant has taken her to the hospital and merely by taking her dead body to the hospital by the applicant, it cannot be said that applicant was having any good intention.
11.

He further submits that although from the account statement of the deceased it appears that about Rs. 1,63,000/- (One lac sixty three thousand) were transferred by the applicant in her account but from her account statement it also reflects that subsequently number of times some amounts were transferred in the account of applicant through NEFT and this fact clearly suggests that Nitin Gautam vs State Of U.P. on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196046175/
2 applicant was using the account of his wife i.e. deceased and therefore, merely due to the deposit of some amount in the account of the deceased it cannot be said that applicant deposited the amount in the account of the deceased with intention that deceased may use the same rather account statement of the deceased shows that actually applicant was the person who was using the account of the deceased.
12.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
13. Applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died within four years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry.

Further, from the FIR although, it reflects that there was no specific demand of dowry was disclosed but subsequently when second statement of the informant was recorded by the Investigating Officer then he categorically stated that applicant and his parents demanded a car and due to that reason they harassed her.

14. As far as argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no evidence that soon before her death deceased was ever tortured by the applicant due to demand of dowry, in this regard, this Court is of the view that this fact can only be properly ascertained by the trial court during the course of trial and at this stage this Court cannot record any finding in this regard.

15. Further, learned counsel for the applicant vehemently submitted that it is a case of suicidal death as autopsy report of the deceased suggests that she died due to hanging and her hyoid bone was also found intact but suicidal death of the wife also attracts the provisions of Section 304B IPC and there is burden on the applicant to explain the abnormal death of his wife.

Although applicant in paragraph-3 of the supplementary affidavit dated 17.07.2023 tried to explain the death of his wife by making averment that due to cooking of food some dispute arose between husband and wife and thereafter deceased locked herself inside the room and subsequently committed suicide.

16. In view of this Court, the defence taken by the applicant appears to be quite vague and general in nature and merely on the basis of such vague and general defence the allegation made against the applicant cannot be completely disbelieved at this stage.

17. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant, who is husband, is not entitled to be released on bail at this stage.
18. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected at this stage.

19. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
